3  COMMON ORDER

These writ petitions have been filed seeking for issuance of a writ of mandamus, directing the first respondent to consider the petitioners' claim petitions filed under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956, on 25.6.2023, 23.1.2024 and 10.1.2024 and to reconsider the Awards dated 15.3.2022, 22.8.2023 and 16.8.2023, respectively and to pay compensation on the proper re-valuation and enhance the compensation in respect of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos. 6299 and 6301 of 2024 subject properties by following the procedure contemplated under Sections 26 to 30 of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013 (Central Act 30 of 2013) and Sections 18 to 27 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996.

2. The main grievance of the petitioners is that even though they have filed claim petitions on 25.6.2023, 23.1.2024 and 10.1.2024, till date, the first respondent has not taken any action on the said claim petitions.
3.
Heard both sides and perused the materials available record.

4. Since these writ petitions are filed for Mandamus simpliciter, to direct the first respondent to consider the claim petitions of the petitioners, this Court, without expressing any view or opinion with regard to the merits of the case, directs the first respondent to consider the claim petitions of the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P.Nos. 6299 and 6301 of 2024 petitioners dated 25.6.2023,
23.1.2024 and 10.1.2024 and pass appropriate orders on merits and in accordance with law, after giving due opportunity of hearing to the petitioners as well as interested parties if any, as the case may be, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
5. With the above directions, these writ petitions are disposed of.
Consequently, connected W.M.P.Nos.7008 and 7003 are closed.
However, there shall be no order as to costs.
6. W.M.P.No.7000 of 2024 is ordered on payment of separate Court fees by each of the petitioners.
